visuals.examples: Source comparisons and reading prompts; no invented measurements or numerical chart.

meaningEvidence: Full original-audio transcript reviewed. At 0–35s the creator discusses a Basel fountain, dragons and Albanian mythological figures; the caption alone does not disclose the panda claim.

At 35–97s the creator repeats a theory that pandas could not exist naturally and were genetically invented in China, connecting this to the circulation of pandas internationally. The article explicitly corrects the theory.
Original poster visually inspected: green basilisk fountain, river and trees behind, creator inset. Exact street and manufacture date are not established.
limitations: ASR is noisy. Article reports the clear argument without treating uncertain lines as verbatim quotation.
The mythical creature and the real animal require different evidence. No biological existence or eighteenth-century extinction date is asserted for a legendary basilisk or dragon.
The 6–7-million-year fossil argument concerns a panda ancestor and feeding adaptation, not the age of the living species.
No unverified demographic total, historical fountain date, or assertion that every international panda arrangement is a diplomatic gift is included.
